by_task.when: When ARIZONA is allowable and an asset matches an Arizona homestead, household-goods, firearm, or motor-vehicle category.
by_task.procedure: Use the substantive asset exemption: § 33-1101(A) for a qualifying occupied homestead, § 33-1123 for household furniture, goods, electronics, or appliances, § 33-1125(10) for firearms, and § 33-1125(8) for motor vehicles. A stated value above the statutory ceiling still permits the EC citation.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not cite § 33-1101(B) or § 33-1121 merely because the debtors are married. Do not treat jewelry as wearing apparel under § 33-1125(1).

by_task.when: When ARIZONA is allowable and an asset is tested against an Arizona substantive exemption.
by_task.procedure:
Match the asset before valuing it: use § 33-1101(A) for an occupied homestead, § 33-1123 for household furniture, goods, electronics, or appliances, § 33-1125(1) for actual wearing apparel, (4) only for engagement or wedding rings, (6) for one watch, (8) for one motor vehicle, (9) for a professionally prescribed prosthesis or physician-authorized mobility or respiratory aid, (10) for firearms, and (11) for domestic animals or household pets. For the whole named asset use the smaller of its value and $400,000 under § 33-1101(A), $15,000 under § 33-1123 or (8), $500 under (1), $2,000 under (4) or (10), or $250 under (6). The supplied provisions state no dollar ceiling for qualifying property under (9) or (11).
Execution example: Hypothetically, a necklace that is neither an engagement nor wedding ring has an empty Arizona array; its ability to be worn does not create a § 33-1125(1) object. An actual coat may instead receive § 33-1125(1), limited to the smaller of its whole value and $500.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not cite § 33-1101(B) or § 33-1121 as an asset exemption. Do not classify jewelry, a prescribed medical device, or another item as household goods merely because it is kept at home. A pendant, necklace, bracelet, cocktail ring, or anniversary ring is not wearing apparel and does not qualify as an engagement or wedding ring without those facts.

operations.rationale: The parent correctly excluded comparable pendants in cases 230 and 231 but, in case 239, emitted § 33-1125(1) for another necklace despite the existing exclusion. A compact deidentified output example reinforces the already-correct Arizona boundary without changing EC or unrelated rules.

diagnoses.rule_anchor: A pendant, necklace, bracelet, cocktail ring, or anniversary ring is not wearing apparel and does not qualify as an engagement or wedding ring without those facts.
